_comment: Pre-registered per-fault target-metric panel (fault_catalog.md §6 realized). For each fault, the Prometheus signal(s) that MUST move if the injection actually took effect. verify_injection.py evaluates these over the baseline vs injection windows and writes a confirmed|borderline|unconfirmed verdict. One target per fault is marked canonical=true (drives the verdict); others are corroborating. Direction: 'increase'|'decrease'. threshold_sigma = min standardized delta over baseline stdev; min_fraction = min share of the injection window past the raw threshold. These are QC gates, NOT the study's modality claims (those live in fault_catalog.md). | 5 Sept 2026: entries for the ten new fault families added, every threshold MEASURED with faults/measure_targets.sh on both applications rather than written from the mechanism. Two calibration passes were needed: the first found cAdvisor's process metric group disabled by default, the second found those same metrics reading 0.0000 without pid:host. A metric that exists and is always zero is more dangerous than one that is missing.

_windows._settle_note: skip the first 30s of the injection window when scoring: 1m-rate-windowed metrics take ~a rate-window to ramp after onset. Campaign runs should use INJECTION_S >= 120 so a clean settled segment remains.

_metric_naming: CALIBRATED 2026-07-28 against the live stack. Request-duration metric name differs by service runtime: Go/Node services (catalogue, frontend) expose 'http_request_duration_seconds'; Java/Spring services (cart, orders, payment, user, shipping) expose 'request_duration_seconds'. Prometheus job labels are singular for carts ('cart'). cAdvisor container 'name' labels are 'docker-compose_<svc>_1'; carts=docker-compose_carts_1 (regex '.*carts_1$' excludes carts-db). NOTE: this cAdvisor build exposes NO cfs-throttle metric, so svc_cpu_cap verifies via app latency, not throttle counters.

slow_db_catalogue.name: catalogue_p95_latency
slow_db_catalogue.why: added DB latency inflates catalogue request duration; DB container metrics stay flat (blind spot)

error_storm_catalogue.name: catalogue_5xx_rate
error_storm_catalogue.why: broken DB connections surface as 5xx on catalogue-backed routes

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: throttled service serves requests slower (this cadvisor build has no cfs-throttle metric, so latency is the QC signal)

svc_cpu_cap_carts.name: carts_cpu_usage_capped
svc_cpu_cap_carts.why: usage pinned at/below the imposed quota

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_memory_limit_dropped
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: the cap is applied: limit drops from host-total (~42GB) to the cap (<=300MB). Reliable for both intensities. (usage/limit ratio is unusable: uncapped baseline limit = host total.) carts working set is ~545MB, so any cap <=300MB necessarily constrains it.

svc_mem_cap_carts.name: carts_oom_kills
svc_mem_cap_carts.why: aggressive cap (160MB, below the working set) forces OOM kills; subtle cap causes GC pressure without necessarily OOMing

dependency_outage_payment.name: payment_cpu_drops
dependency_outage_payment.why:
MEASURED 5 Sept on campaign run r1: payment CPU 0.00316 -> 0.000603 cores, direction correct, 95% of injection samples past the threshold. Read `borderline` on sigma alone.
The 2-sigma gate is UNSATISFIABLE: baseline 0.00316 with std 0.00197, so -2 sigma demands -0.0008 cores. CPU cannot be negative. A paused container's CPU can only fall to zero, which for this metric is barely 1.6 sigma away from where it starts. Lowered to 1.0 - a reachable gate. The coverage test is doing the real work here, and it is the right test: the container is paused, so its CPU should sit at the floor for essentially the whole window, which is what 95% coverage says.
METRICS-WEAK fault (calibrated: payment baseline CPU ~0.004 core drops ~58% to ~0.0018 under pause, smeared by the 1m rate window; may verify BORDERLINE). This aligns with fault_catalog.md: TRACES win this fault (the broken orders->payment edge), not metrics. See orders_5xx note below.

dependency_outage_payment.name: orders_5xx_rate_EXPECTED_BLIND
dependency_outage_payment.why: CALIBRATION FINDING: stays ~0. docker pause FREEZES payment, so orders' HTTP call HANGS (blocked socket read) rather than fail-fast - the request never completes with an error status inside the window. A frozen dependency is metrics/logs-INVISIBLE while the kernel sees orders threads blocked in read() on the payment socket. This is a concrete instance of the study's kernel-wins thesis; kept as documentation, not a verification gate.

queue_backlog.name: queue_master_cpu_drops
queue_backlog.why: calibrated: queue-master baseline CPU ~0.008 core drops ~77% to ~0.0019 under pause (1m-rate-smeared). METRICS-WEAK silent-failure fault: orders keep succeeding, no error anywhere; the real signal is the KERNEL (queue-master cgroup goes quiet while rabbitmq keeps taking inbound) - matches fault_catalog.md's kernel-wins prediction.

noisy_neighbor.name: neighbor_cpu_active
noisy_neighbor.why: CALIBRATED & PREMISE VALIDATED (subtle, 1.0-cpu cap): neighbor consumes ~0.75 core (fired; host CPU 28%->45%) while service KPIs stay within normal variance - carts p95 21.8ms->23.1ms (+6%), catalogue p95 4.75ms->4.75ms (0%). The kernel-only showcase: CPU contention is host/kernel-visible but app-metric-blind. This target verifies the fault FIRED; the KPIs-stay-flat premise is the study finding, not a verification gate.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_ops
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED 5 Sept during campaign run anomaly_disk_r5: 578 -> 2058 writes/s (3.56x). Replaces rate(node_disk_io_time_seconds_total[1m]), which failed on all five repeats with a ratio of 0.95x - not because the fault was weak but because io_time is a UTILISATION metric and utilisation was already spoken for. LTTng writes the kernel trace continuously throughout every run at ~53 MB/s, which is exactly the measured baseline of node_disk_written_bytes_total, so the disk is near-saturated before the fault starts and 'fraction of time busy' has nowhere left to climb. Unbounded counters - operations, bytes, queue depth - show the fault plainly.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_queue_depth
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED: 5.49 -> 12.95 (2.36x). Weighted io_time is queue depth x time, so unlike plain io_time it keeps rising after the device is already busy.

anomaly_disk.name: host_disk_write_bytes
anomaly_disk.why: MEASURED: 53.3 -> 133.4 MB/s (2.50x). The 53.3 MB/s baseline is the kernel trace itself.

anomaly_mem.name: host_mem_available_drop
anomaly_mem.why: MEASURED 5 Sept on campaign run anomaly_mem_r1: available goes 0.79 -> 0.40 (33.7 GB -> 19.9 GB), sigma -14.6. The previous entry demanded < 0.25 and its own comment said 'Finalize on VM calibration' - nobody did, and 0.25 is unreachable: stress-ng vm-hang asks for 88% of RAM but MemAvailable bottoms out near 0.40. All four collected repeats read unconfirmed on fraction alone, with direction correct and sigma at -14.6. min_fraction is 0.5 rather than 0.8 because the allocation RAMPS - the first part of the injection window is still filling, so early samples legitimately sit above any floor. A threshold that assumes a step change cannot score a fault that ramps.

anomaly_mem.name: host_major_page_faults
anomaly_mem.why: MEASURED: 0 -> 73/s. The system is genuinely short of memory and going to disk for pages, which is the consequence that matters rather than the allocation itself.

anomaly_net.name: catalogue_p95_latency_net
anomaly_net.why: CALIBRATED (wave-2): host-bridge netem (100ms delay + 3% loss on br-<compose>) inflates every inter-service hop; catalogue p95 (front-end->catalogue->DB) rises. node-NIC throughput is NOT a reliable signal for added latency (internal bridge traffic doesn't traverse the physical NIC).

svc_net_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_net_carts.why: per-container netem inside carts' netns inflates carts request latency; single-service impairment (front-end sees it upstream). Calibrate on the VM.

lock_contention.name: lock_contention_threads
lock_contention.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 17 threads on both applications, and the series does not exist before injection, so the baseline is 0. A co-located workload fault is confirmed by the workload being there and doing its characteristic thing; the contention itself is a kernel claim, not a metrics one.

lock_contention.name: lock_contention_cpu
lock_contention.why: MEASURED: 1.03 cores Sock Shop, 0.95 Train Ticket, against a 1.0 cap.

priority_inversion.name: priority_inversion_cpu
priority_inversion.why: MEASURED: 1.03 cores Sock Shop, 0.98 Train Ticket. The inversion itself is only visible in the wait times the workload reports and in the kernel stream.

deadlock.name: deadlock_threads
deadlock.why: MEASURED: 25 threads on both applications. CPU is deliberately NOT a target here - it reads 0.0001, because deadlocked threads consume nothing. That is the fault's whole character and the reason it is hard: a stuck system looks like an idle one.

fd_exhaustion.name: front_end_restart_loop
fd_exhaustion.note: REPLACED 2026-09-16 after measuring all 5 re-collected runs. The old target summed a series that is not one series: container_file_descriptors{name=~'.*front-end_1$'} matches ELEVEN series for one container, differing only in container_label_restartcount, because cAdvisor mints a new series on every restart. Summing them produced injection_mean=446 and recovery_mean=560 against a baseline of 98, so a 'decrease' target failed and the run read unconfirmed. The single continuous series is flat (98 -> 96 -> 96); nothing climbed, the SERIES COUNT grew. What the fault actually does is restart-loop the front-end: restartcount runs 21->31 in a 120 s injection, and the count of NEW restart generations inside the injection window is EXACTLY 9 in all five runs. Control: lock_contention r2-r5 sit at 76->76 with zero restarts, so the front-end is stable when nothing attacks it; dns_delay shows 9,0,8,0,0, so the signal is not unique to this fault but is decisive for it. CAVEAT: the loop outlives the injection (Docker restart backoff), so each run's BASELINE inherits the previous run's tail - 1,6,7,11,12 new generations in the five baselines. Judge on generations that START inside the injection window, not on a baseline-relative ratio.

conn_pool_exhaustion.name: db_sockets_held
conn_pool_exhaustion.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 4 -> 154 sockets on Sock Shop (38.5x) and 204 -> 2005 on Train Ticket (9.8x). The strongest signal of the whole panel, and it comes from the server rather than from the holder.

resource_abuse.name: resource_abuse_cpu
resource_abuse.why: MEASURED: 1.01 cores Sock Shop, 0.97 Train Ticket. Volume of CPU is the only thing metrics can see; whether it is ABUSE rather than work is the question the study asks, and no metric answers it.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_out
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED 5 Sept: 42.0 MB/s on both applications. This read 0.0000 until the recipe was changed to send to a separate sink container - the first version sent to 127.0.0.1 inside its own container, so 839 MB crossed no interface and no counter saw it.

data_exfiltration.name: exfil_bytes_in_at_sink
data_exfiltration.why: MEASURED: 41.7 MB/s Sock Shop, 42.0 Train Ticket. The receiving end, on purpose - the sender's own claim was 839 MB and was true while nothing left the container.

fork_storm.name: fork_storm_processes
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 201 processes on both applications. Per-container rather than host-wide, which matters: node_forks_total is 12.2x on Sock Shop but only 7.2x on Train Ticket, and in an earlier pass 1.05x, because TT already forks ~112/s from 40 JVMs and Nacos health checks. A host counter cannot serve both applications; this one does.

fork_storm.name: host_fork_rate
fork_storm.why: MEASURED: 8.7 -> 106.5/s Sock Shop (12.2x), 15.7 -> 113.1 Train Ticket (7.2x). Corroborating only - see above for why it cannot be canonical.

nagle_delayed_ack.name: nagle_workload_present
nagle_delayed_ack.why: MEASURED: 1.00 cores on both. This is a PRESENCE check and nothing more. The fault's actual signature - a ~99 ms stall clustered within 1 ms of itself, against a TCP_NODELAY control at 0.51 ms in the same run - is invisible to every metric we collect, which is precisely why the family is in the catalogue.

dns_delay.name: dns_delay_no_metric_signature
dns_delay.why: REGISTERED AS A KNOWN NEGATIVE. Two calibration passes found nothing that moves: host UDP counters 1.00x, front-end receive rate 0.58-0.83x (down, not up). The fault is real - the iptables rule drops 24 queries while the app runs, wall-clock time goes 914 ms -> 20,034 ms and 31 of 400 requests fail - but p50 reads 3.9 ms and p95 8.0 ms, BOTH BETTER than baseline. It hides in the tail, where no aggregate metric looks. Expect this check to fail; the failure is the finding, and verify_injection will report borderline rather than silently passing.

code_lock_across_io.name: catalogue_throughput_flat_expected
code_lock_across_io.note: MEASURED FLAT, 2026-09-15. Plotted across a whole run, catalogue request rate is 264.1/s at injection start and 263.7/s at injection end - unchanged. The 0.2 -> 262 step happens FORTY SECONDS EARLIER and is the load generator spinning up (CAMPAIGN-ISSUES 20). An earlier version of this target was set to expect that rise and 'confirmed' runs on it, which detected the load generator rather than the fault. The defect is real - the smoke test measures 4.00x slowdown - but no Prometheus series moves with it. Injection and recovery means are equal (within 1%), which is the load ramp and not the fault. Two SIBLING families (code_event_loop_block, code_serial_awaits) DO move this metric - they are front-end Node defects that stall a single-threaded event loop, whereas this one is Go in catalogue where concurrency absorbs the per-request slowdown. Marked expected_to_fail so this reports no_metric_signature, which is a finding, not a broken run.

code_n_plus_one.name: catalogue_throughput_flat_expected
code_n_plus_one.note: MEASURED FLAT, 2026-09-15. Plotted across a whole run, catalogue request rate is 264.1/s at injection start and 263.7/s at injection end - unchanged. The 0.2 -> 262 step happens FORTY SECONDS EARLIER and is the load generator spinning up (CAMPAIGN-ISSUES 20). An earlier version of this target was set to expect that rise and 'confirmed' runs on it, which detected the load generator rather than the fault. The defect is real - the smoke test measures 5.33x slowdown - but no Prometheus series moves with it. Injection and recovery means are equal (within 1%), which is the load ramp and not the fault. Two SIBLING families (code_event_loop_block, code_serial_awaits) DO move this metric - they are front-end Node defects that stall a single-threaded event loop, whereas this one is Go in catalogue where concurrency absorbs the per-request slowdown. Marked expected_to_fail so this reports no_metric_signature, which is a finding, not a broken run.

code_event_loop_block.name: catalogue_throughput_drop
code_event_loop_block.note: MEASURED VISIBLE, 2026-09-15 (5 runs). Catalogue request rate falls to 0.27-0.39x of baseline during injection and recovers to 122-134/s afterwards, with the same image running throughout - only the /dev/shm flag changed. Smoke test measures 43.12x slowdown. This is a front-end (Node) defect: the event loop is single-threaded, so blocking it stalls every request and catalogue stops being called. NOTE the sigma test fails here (sigma_ok=false) because the baseline window includes the load generator ramping up, which inflates baseline_std - see CAMPAIGN-ISSUES 20. The verdict rests on direction plus fraction, corroborated by the recovery window.

code_serial_awaits.name: catalogue_throughput_drop
code_serial_awaits.note: MEASURED VISIBLE, 2026-09-15 (5 runs). Catalogue request rate falls to 0.52-0.54x of baseline during injection and recovers to 127-136/s afterwards, with the same image running throughout - only the /dev/shm flag changed. Smoke test measures 18.99x slowdown. This is a front-end (Node) defect: the event loop is single-threaded, so blocking it stalls every request and catalogue stops being called. NOTE the sigma test fails here (sigma_ok=false) because the baseline window includes the load generator ramping up, which inflates baseline_std - see CAMPAIGN-ISSUES 20. The verdict rests on direction plus fraction, corroborated by the recovery window.

code_unbounded_cache.name: catalogue_throughput_flat_expected
code_unbounded_cache.note: MEASURED FLAT, 2026-09-15. Plotted across a whole run, catalogue request rate is 264.1/s at injection start and 263.7/s at injection end - unchanged. The 0.2 -> 262 step happens FORTY SECONDS EARLIER and is the load generator spinning up (CAMPAIGN-ISSUES 20). An earlier version of this target was set to expect that rise and 'confirmed' runs on it, which detected the load generator rather than the fault. The defect is real - the smoke test measures memory growth with latency flat at 1.00x - but no Prometheus series moves with it. Injection and recovery means are equal (within 1%), which is the load ramp and not the fault. Two SIBLING families (code_event_loop_block, code_serial_awaits) DO move this metric - they are front-end Node defects that stall a single-threaded event loop, whereas this one is Go in catalogue where concurrency absorbs the per-request slowdown. Marked expected_to_fail so this reports no_metric_signature, which is a finding, not a broken run.

code_unbounded_cache.name: front_end_memory_growth
code_unbounded_cache.note: Recorded, not decisive. The defect never frees, so memory is its only signal - but over a 120 s window the growth is small against a 40 GB host, which is why it cannot carry the verdict.

code_lock_contended.name: catalogue_p95_latency
code_lock_contended.note: v3, 2026-11-24. Same defect as code_lock_across_io, collected with a constant 5 ms database delay and 40 list requests/s directly on the catalogue, so the lock is contended (run_family.sh). PREDICTED from the calibration, to be confirmed on the first run: list requests queue behind one mutex (the extra clients measured a median of 24 ms off and 80 ms on), so catalogue p95 rises by at least 20 ms at injection and falls back at recovery. An earlier setup with 20 unpaced clients made p95 FALL at injection, because the lock throttled the load itself.

svc_cpuset_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
svc_cpuset_carts.why: v3, 2026-11-24. All threads of the service share one core and wait for each other. Calibrated on the VM under the 150-user load: carts p95 23.8 ms with all 12 cores, 153.7 ms on one core, 23.8 ms after the restore (two cores: 39.8 ms, below this threshold - the subtle setting is expected to read borderline).

disk_full_carts-db.name: carts_p95_latency_flat_expected
disk_full_carts-db.note: v3, MEASURED 2026-11-24 in calibration: no metric sees this fault. With its volume full the database (MongoDB 3.4) keeps serving, aborts about once a minute (Invariant failure ... No space left on device, signal 6) and is restarted by docker in about 2 s. Over a 1-minute rate window carts p95 stays at 22-23 ms (20-second windows show 1.1 s spikes at each crash); carts 5xx has no series; the database's memory, threads, write rate and CPU do not move; container_start_time does not change on a restart; node-exporter does not see the loop-mounted volume. Marked expected_to_fail so the run reads no_metric_signature. THE CHECK THAT THE FAULT HAPPENED IS IN run_family.sh: the database's own log in the bundle must contain 'No space left on device' and at least one abort inside the injection window.

port_exhaustion_catalogue.name: catalogue_5xx_rate
port_exhaustion_catalogue.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25 on the VM under the 150-user load: with 200 local ports left the catalogue's new database connections fail with 'cannot assign requested address' (1,835 log lines in 80 s) and its 5xx rate goes 0.0 -> 7-12/s of 257 requests/s, back to 0.0 within 20 s of the restore. Normal use: about 1,700 sockets in TIME_WAIT. The front-end shows no 5xx and no latency change. (1,500 ports: nothing for a minute, then a burst of 125/s - the subtle setting is late and uneven.)

pid_limit_orders.name: frontend_5xx_rate
pid_limit_orders.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25 on the VM under the 150-user load: with orders limited to its current task count the kernel refuses about 16 thread creations per second, orders logs 6,372 'unable to create new native thread' lines in 100 s, and the front-end's 5xx rate goes 0.0 -> 15-16/s (placing an order fails), back to 0.0 within 20 s of the restore. The orders service's own request metric shows no non-2xx at all, so the front-end series is the target. Headroom 8 (subtle): no effect.

db_table_lock_catalogue.name: catalogue_p95_latency
db_table_lock_catalogue.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25 on the VM under the 150-user load: with the catalogue's three tables write-locked 2 s out of every 3 s, catalogue p95 goes 4.8 ms -> 2,290 ms and its request rate 262 -> 122/s; no 5xx anywhere; back to 4.8 ms within 20 s of the cleanup. The database reached its 151-connection limit but refused no connection. Subtle (0.3 s of every 3 s): p95 about 165 ms, rate unchanged. CHANGED 2026-11-25: abs_threshold 0.5 -> 0.05 s, because subtle run 1 (25-11-2026, 0.3 s of every 3 s): catalogue p95 0.145 s mean over the fault, never above the old bar of 0.5 s, so it read 'unconfirmed' although the spans show p95 3.9 -> 176 ms. The catalogue's baseline p95 is 4.8 ms, so 0.05 s is still 10 times it.

slow_client_carts.name: frontend_request_rate
slow_client_carts.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25: with the carts service's 200 worker threads held, every simulated user ends up stuck in a cart call and the front-end's rate falls from about 290/s to under 20/s within 20 s and to 0 within a minute; back within 20 s of the cleanup. The carts service's OWN metrics cannot be the target: its /metrics endpoint is served by the same stuck threads, so Prometheus gets no samples from it during the fault (second check run: 0 finite samples, scored 'unconfirmed'). That gap in the carts series is itself a sign of the fault.

slow_client_carts.name: cart_scrape_up
slow_client_carts.why: the carts service stops answering its metrics scrape while its worker threads are held

net_bandwidth_catalogue.name: catalogue_p95_latency
net_bandwidth_catalogue.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25 on the VM under the 150-user load. The catalogue sends a little over 4 Mbit/s. Cap 4 Mbit/s: p95 4.8 -> 415 ms, rate 260 -> 231/s. Cap 2 Mbit/s (aggressive): p50 2.5 -> 240 ms, p95 -> 2.0 s, rate -> 140/s. Cap 1 Mbit/s: p50 1.2 s, rate 70/s, 34 packets dropped in 80 s. No 5xx at any setting; back to 4.8 ms within 20 s of removing the cap. CHANGED 2026-11-25: abs_threshold 0.3 -> 0.05 s, because the subtle setting (4 Mbit/s) gave p95 about 0.4 s in calibration, too close to the old bar of 0.3 s. The catalogue's baseline p95 is 4.8 ms, so 0.05 s is still 10 times it.

cpu_weight_carts.name: carts_p95_latency
cpu_weight_carts.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-25 on the VM, 150 users, with a neighbour of 12 busy processes for the whole run: carts at cpu.weight 10 goes from p95 88 ms to 3.0-4.2 s and from 91 to 66 requests/s, no 5xx; back to 85 ms within 40 s of restoring weight 100. CHANGED 2026-11-26 before the subtle runs: abs_threshold 0.5 -> 0.2 s. Subtle (weight 30) measured: carts p95 about 90 ms with the neighbour alone, 250-640 ms at weight 30 (30 s windows), so 0.5 s would miss part of it. 0.2 s is about twice the busy baseline.

port_scan_front-end.name: frontend_p95_latency_flat_expected
port_scan_front-end.note: v3, MEASURED 2026-11-25 in calibration: no metric and no log line sees this fault. 200 connection attempts per second from the front-end's address to ports 1-1024 of the 15 other containers (19,253 tried in 96 s, 16 open, 19,237 refused): catalogue and front-end rate, errors and answer times unchanged, host 48% -> 50% busy, 0 log lines about refused or reset connections in any service. Marked expected_to_fail so the run reads no_metric_signature; the proof that the scan ran is the scanner's own count in the run log, checked by run_family.sh, and the refused connects in the kernel trace.

code_spin_loop.name: catalogue_p95_latency
code_spin_loop.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load, image swapped before the load started. spin_loop: catalogue p95 4.8 -> 21 ms, CPU 0.14 -> 0.79 cores, rate unchanged, nothing fails; back at once after cleanup.

code_thread_leak.name: catalogue_go_threads
code_thread_leak.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load, image swapped before the load started. thread_leak: catalogue threads 17 -> 147, 361, 580 at +30, +60, +90 s (about 7 per second); answer times, rates and errors unchanged. The leaked threads stay after cleanup (678), so the recovery window does NOT recover - by design; the process is restarted by disarm after tracing.

code_large_payload.name: catalogue_network_transmit
code_large_payload.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load, image swapped before the load started. large_payload: the catalogue sends 2.8 -> 18.1-18.9 Mbit/s (interface counter), about 0.36 -> 2.4 MB/s in the cAdvisor series; answer times, rates and errors unchanged.

code_regex_backtrack.name: frontend_p95_latency
code_regex_backtrack.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load, image swapped before the load started. regex_backtrack:26:0.002: front-end p95 66-76 -> 187-204 ms, p50 unchanged, rate 291 -> 153-238/s; back at once after cleanup. 27:0.005 grew to 764 ms within 90 s and still rising (an outage in the making), not used.

rt_hog.name: last_cpu_idle
rt_hog.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load. rt_hog: the last CPU (11 on this 12-CPU VM) goes from about 57% to 100% busy; no service's rate, errors or answer time move (front-end p95 even lower, noise). A host-metric and kernel family. The target assumes the recipe's default RT_CPU = nproc - 1 = 11.

mtu_blackhole_catalogue.name: catalogue_5xx_rate
mtu_blackhole_catalogue.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load. mtu_blackhole (576 on the host side): the catalogue answers EVERY request with 5xx (100-255 per second, 0 before), not only large ones as predicted: the database's answers TO the catalogue are large too and are dropped, so its queries fail. Retransmitted segments of the catalogue 9 -> 160. The errors last about 60-90 s after the MTU is restored, so the recovery window still shows them.

login_bruteforce.name: user_500_rate
login_bruteforce.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load. login_bruteforce: 2,134 wrong-password logins in 120 s, all refused; the user service answers each with 500 (0 -> 20-24 per second) and logs 'err=Unauthorized'; the front-end returns 401 to the client but has no 401 series in its metrics. No other service moves.

unexpected_exec_front-end.name: frontend_p95_latency_flat_expected
unexpected_exec_front-end.note: v3, calibrated 2026-11-26 on the VM under the 150-user load. unexpected_exec: 4 rounds of a read-only shell in the front-end in 90 s; no metric moves. Marked expected_to_fail so the run reads no_metric_signature; the proof is the round count in the run log (run_family.sh checks it) and the exec events in the kernel trace.

code_fd_leak.name: catalogue_open_fds
code_fd_leak.why: v3, calibrated 2026-11-27 on the VM under the 150-user load, image swapped before the load started. fd_leak: catalogue descriptors 17 -> 105, 191, 278 at +30, +60, +90 s (about 3 per second); rates, answer times and errors unchanged.
